cards.name: Rolling end credits (AE scroll)
cards.summary: A centred credit list scrolls up the screen at a constant whole-pixel speed, from below the frame until the last line has left the top.
avoid: text under about 30 px tall at 1080p: thin strokes shimmer while moving
speeds that are not a whole number of pixels per frame (judder)
cards.keyframes_note: Scenes for vfx.render_scenes(scenes, aep, out_dir) at its defaults (1920x1080, 25 fps); segs are [t0, v0, t1, v1, ease] in comp seconds with ease lin | smooth | out | in (ae_lib.jsx seg). One box-text layer ([1400, 2200] box, '\r' between lines) moved by a LINEAR position seg from y 2280 to -1200: 3480 px in 34.8 s = 100 px/s = 4 px per frame at 25 fps. Whole pixels per frame avoid the stutter of fractional steps; the speed itself is a working default (about 3-4 px/frame at 1080p keeps 44 px text readable), not a standard. The box must contain every line (box text clips what does not fit) and the start/end positions assume the block is at most about 2200 px tall: recompute both for longer lists. Two-column credits (role right-aligned, name left-aligned) need two text layers; vfx_build.jsx text supports left or centre justification only. Premiere's own route is the Essential Graphics Roll option ('Rolling credits and crawls in Premiere'). Measured 2026-10-13: 4 px per frame on every one of 722 frame pairs, as planned.

verified.note: The centred list rolls up from below the frame until the last line leaves the top; measured 4 px per frame on all 722 frame pairs with text (constant, whole pixels).

cards.name: News ticker crawl (looping)
cards.summary: A red ticker band along the bottom with a white BREAKING label box and headlines crawling right to left in an endless seamless loop, rendered with alpha for overlay.
use_for: running headlines under a live-style segment
avoid: reels: the bottom 20-35% of a 9:16 frame sits under platform UI (see 'Platform UI safe zones')
fast crawls: keep it readable (about 6-10 s for a headline to cross)

layers.name: CRAWL
layers.text: <HEADLINE ONE> | <HEADLINE TWO> | <HEADLINE THREE> | <HEADLINE ONE> | <HEADLINE TWO> | <HEADLINE THREE> | <HEADLINE ONE> | <HEADLINE TWO> | <HEADLINE THREE> |

expr.position: var w = sourceRectAtTime(time, false).width; var u = thisComp.layer("CRAWL_UNIT").sourceRectAtTime(time, false).width; var period = (w - u) / 2; [240 + w / 2 - ((time - inPoint) * 200) % period, value[1]]

cards.keyframes_note: Scenes for vfx.render_scenes(scenes, aep, out_dir) at its defaults (1920x1080, 25 fps); segs are [t0, v0, t1, v1, ease] in comp seconds with ease lin | smooth | out | in (ae_lib.jsx seg). The crawl is an expression on Position (not keyframes), so it loops for any duration: the headline string is repeated 3 times and x moves left by (time * 200) modulo one repeat's advance width, which lands the second copy exactly where the first started. That width comes from two ink measurements: (sourceRectAtTime width of the 3-copy CRAWL minus that of the 1-copy CRAWL_UNIT, a hidden copy in the same font and size) / 2. The ink box leaves out the same trailing space and side bearing in both, so they cancel. Measured 2026-10-13 with the old period (ink width / 3): 8 px per frame on 499 frame pairs, but the band jumped 13 px at every wrap (frames 149, 299 and 448, every 5.99 s). Ink width / 3 was 5 px short of one repeat. Fix applied 2026-10-14, not re-rendered. 200 px/s = 8 px per frame at 25 fps (whole pixels). The text is clipped to the band right of the label by an alpha track matte (CRAWL_MATTE, hidden automatically). The band sits at y 960-1040: inside action safe (bottom 38 px) and clear of title safe for 1920x1080. 'alpha': true renders a .mov with alpha for overlay in Premiere. Keep CRAWL_UNIT's text exactly one repeat of CRAWL's (same font, size and tracking).

verified.note: The band, label and crawl look right and the crawl moves a steady 8 px per frame, but at every wrap (frames 149, 299, 448) the text jumps 13 px: the loop is not seamless.

previous.why: loop period now (3-copy width - 1-copy width) / 2 from a hidden CRAWL_UNIT text layer, see keyframes_note; not rendered again
